title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
title_zh: BrickBench: 评估代理型砖设计

paragraphs.en: GPT-6 Astra Claude Opus 5.5 Qwen 3.8 Flash Gemini 3.8 Flash Muse Spark 1.3

paragraphs.en: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. We score validity, alignment, and design across three settings that vary in scale and part availability. We provide BrickAgent, an environment for coding agents to construct, inspect, and validate their designs. We find that leading agents largely satisfy verifiable physical and semantic requirements, but fall short of human designs. We release our benchmark and environment at http://www.brickben.ch
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 BrickBench，一个用于智能体文本条件化乐高套装设计的基准测试。 给定一个提示，智能体的任务是生成一个既能满足语义和设计标准，又能实际搭建的组装方案。 为此，它必须从离散的零件库中选择零件，并同时对局部和全局约束进行推理。 我们在三种规模和零件可用性各异的设置中，对有效性、一致性和设计进行了评分。 我们提供了 BrickAgent，一个供编码智能体构建、检查和验证其设计的环境。 我们发现，领先的智能体基本能满足可验证的物理和语义要求，但尚未达到人类设计的水平。 我们在 http://www.brickben.ch 发布了我们的基准测试和环境。

paragraphs.en: Designing a LEGO assembly is deceptively difficult. A designer must select from thousands of parts, arrange them into a recognizable form, and ensure that the structure holds together. Computational generative approaches to brick assembly have relied on specialized models and carefully engineered representations to handle these challenges ( Chung et al., 2021 ; Pun et al., 2025 ; Kulits & Schmid, 2026 ) . But coding agents offer a different approach: they can write programs, execute them, inspect the results, and revise. This shift is already transforming software engineering ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , graphics ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , and CAD ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . We find that a general coding agent, without task-specific training, substantially outperforms specialized LEGO-generation models on the BrickNet benchmark ( Kulits & Schmid, 2026 ) , approaching the semantic alignment of its reference assemblies ( Fig. 2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 设计乐高拼装结构看似简单，实则极具挑战性。 设计师必须从数千个零件中挑选，将它们组合成可识别的形状，并确保整个结构能够稳固结合。 基于计算的乐高砖块生成方法一直依赖专门的模型和精心设计的表示方式来应对这些挑战（Chung 等，2021；Pun 等，2025；Kulits & Schmid，2026）。 但编码智能体提供了一种不同的方法：它们可以编写程序、执行程序、检查结果并进行修改。 这种转变已经正在改变软件工程（Jimenez 等，2024）、图形学（Gu 等，2025）和计算机辅助设计（Zhang 等，2026）。 我们发现，一个无需任务特定训练的通用编码智能体，在 BrickNet 基准测试中的表现显著优于专门的乐高生成模型（Kulits & Schmid，2026），其语义对齐程度接近参考拼装结构（图 2）。

paragraphs.en: Yet does this mean agents have learned to design LEGO? Existing evaluations leave two important challenges unexplored. First, physical complexity: BrickNet evaluates small objects of at most 100 parts, far from the hundreds or thousands of interconnected pieces and inventory constraints of a full LEGO set. Second, and more fundamentally, design quality: making an assembly that works is not the same as making an assembly worth building. The appeal of LEGO lies not merely in reproducing an object, but in the creativity of its construction: clever part usage, shapes, proportions, and details. Two builds can be equally valid and faithful to a description, yet differ dramatically in how well they are designed. Unlike physical validity or semantic alignment with a prompt, design quality has no definitive pass/fail test.
paragraphs.zh: 但这是否意味着智能体已经学会了设计乐高？ 现有的评估方法仍有两个重要挑战未被探索。 首先，物理复杂性：BrickNet 评估的物体最多只有 100 个零件，远不及完整乐高套装中成百上千个相互连接的零件和库存限制。 其次，也是更根本的问题，是设计质量：制造一个能正常运作的组合体，并不等同于制造一个值得搭建的组合体。 乐高的魅力不仅在于复现某个物体，更在于其构建过程中的创造力：巧妙运用零件、形状、比例和细节。 两个搭建作品可能同样合理且忠实于描述，但它们在设计水平上可能存在巨大差异。 与物理上的可行性或对提示的语义一致性不同，设计质量并没有明确通过/失败的测试标准。

paragraphs.en: We introduce BrickBench , a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design ( Fig. 1 ). BrickBench contains 300 prompts across three settings: Model (at most 400 parts), Set (400–4000 parts), and Alt-Build (a fixed inventory of parts). To support complex construction, we introduce BrickAgent , an environment for agentic LEGO design including construction tools and interpretable validation of connectivity, collisions, and stability. Rather than prescribing how to design an assembly, BrickAgent provides the building blocks, constraints, and feedback, leaving the agent to devise its own solution. To evaluate what validity and semantic alignment miss, we measure design quality through pairwise judgments, validated against human preferences.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 BrickBench，一个用于智能体文本条件化乐高套装设计的基准测试（图 1）。 BrickBench 包含 300 个提示词，覆盖三种设置：模型（最多 400 个零件）、套装（400–4000 个零件）和替代构建方案（固定库存的零件）。 为支持复杂构建，我们引入了 BrickAgent，一个用于智能体乐高设计的环境，包含构建工具以及对连接性、碰撞和稳定性的可解释验证。 BrickAgent 不会规定如何设计装配体，而是提供基础构件、约束条件和反馈，由智能体自行构思解决方案。 为了评估有效性和语义对齐方面的不足，我们通过成对比较判断来衡量设计质量，并依据人类偏好进行验证。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate eleven frontier agents and two data-driven baselines. With BrickAgent, leading agents produce valid assemblies for nearly every prompt, and the best satisfies approximately 95% of semantic requirements. Removing the environment sharply reduces physical validity, showing that reliable construction depends on grounded tools and feedback. Design quality, however, separates agents far more strongly, and human raters identify human-designed assemblies in 323 of 360 comparisons. These findings reveal a shift in the challenge of LEGO design: Agents are learning to build what works, but not yet what makes a great design.
paragraphs.zh: 我们评估了十一个前沿智能体和两个数据驱动基线模型。 使用 BrickAgent，领先智能体几乎能为每个提示生成有效的组装方案，而表现最佳的智能体能满足约 95% 的语义要求。 移除环境会显著降低物理有效性，这表明可靠的构建依赖于基于现实的工具和反馈。 然而，设计质量在智能体之间的差异更为显著，人类评分者在 360 次比较中识别出了 323 个由人类设计的组装方案。 这些发现揭示了乐高设计挑战的重心正在发生转变：智能体已经学会构建可行的方案，但尚未能创造出卓越的设计。

paragraphs.en: BrickBench , a benchmark of 300 prompts in three settings for agentic brick design, with metrics for physical validity (connections, collisions, and stability under simulation), semantic alignment ( VQA , over yes/no questions decomposed from each prompt), and design quality ( ELO , from pairwise judgments by a VLM validated against human raters).
paragraphs.zh: BrickBench 是一项针对智能体砖块设计的基准测试，包含三种设置下的 300 条提示，并设有以下指标：物理有效性（连接性、碰撞以及模拟环境下的稳定性）、语义对齐（VQA，基于每条提示分解出的“是/否”问题）以及设计质量（ELO，通过经人类评分者验证的视觉语言模型进行成对判断得出）。

paragraphs.en: BrickAgent , an environment enabling coding agents to programmatically construct, inspect, and validate complex LEGO assemblies, with part search, placement by connectors, subassemblies, rendering, and a validator that names parts at fault. paragraphs.zh: BrickAgent 是一个环境，使编码智能体能够以编程方式构建、检查和验证复杂的乐高组件，支持零件搜索、通过连接器进行放置、子组件组装、渲染，并配备一个能指出故障零件的验证器。 如果没有它，有效组件的比例对于 GPT-6 Astra 会从 100% 降至 40%，而对于 GPT-5.6 Luna 则会降至不到 1%。

paragraphs.zh: 对十一个前沿智能体和两个数据驱动基线模型的系统性评估，并通过人类研究验证了设计指标，同时衡量了与人类设计之间的差距。

paragraphs.en: Agentic Benchmarks. Benchmarks for coding agents validate an agent’s work by executing it. SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) runs a repository’s tests on a patch an agent supplied, and OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) tracks state through execution. SceneCraft ( Hu et al., 2024 ) writes Blender scripts, and CAD-Assistant ( Mallis et al., 2025 ) writes CAD programs. Benchmarks then execute the program and score the result. BlenderGym ( Gu et al., 2025 ) compares the result with a goal scene, and BenchCAD ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) executes CadQuery programs for industrial parts. BuildArena ( Xia et al., 2026 ) scores machines assembled from modular parts by their simulated behavior, and PhyBlock ( Ma et al., 2025 ) scores block placements for plausibility in a physics simulator. BrickBench executes the agent’s program into an assembly of real LEGO parts and validates connections, collisions, and stability under simulation.

paragraphs.en: LEGO and Evaluation. Prior work generates LEGO assemblies with learned models and uses LEGO tasks to evaluate others. BrickGPT ( Pun et al., 2025 ) fine-tunes a language model to place eight brick types on a 20 × 20 × 20 20{\times}20{\times}20 grid from a caption. BrickNet ( Kulits & Schmid, 2026 ) , predicts connections rather than positions and autoregressively generates structures through typed connectors. LEGO-Maker ( Ge et al., 2025 ) produces building facades conditioned on an image. Other work evaluates agents and multimodal models on LEGO tasks. Break and Make ( Walsman et al., 2022 ) gives an agent an LDraw model in a simulator to test whether it can inspect it, take it apart, and rebuild it from scratch. LEGO-Puzzles ( Tang et al., 2026 ) presents multimodal models spatial questions about assembly steps. BrickBench does both: general coding agents generate set-scale assemblies from a text prompt, while we score the assemblies on physical validity, prompt alignment, and design.

paragraphs.en: BrickNet ( Kulits & Schmid, 2026 ) annotates each part in the LDraw library with typed connectors. Each connector instance has a type, a subtype, a polarity, and a frame. The subtype names the connector’s geometry within its type and fixes what it mates with: a stud mates with a hole or a tube, and a bar with a clip. The polarity distinguishes the two halves of a hinge, ball, or fixed joint, which must be opposite to connect. The frame is the connector’s position and orientation in the coordinates of its part, with one axis along the direction of mating. Two part instances are connected when a compatible pair of their connectors is aligned up to tolerance.
paragraphs.zh: BrickNet（Kulits & Schmid，2026）为 LDraw 库中的每个零件添加了带类型的连接器标注。 每个连接器实例都具有一个类型、一个子类型、一个极性和一个框架。 子类型指定了连接器在其类型内的几何形状，并决定了其连接对象：凸台与孔或管连接，而杆则与夹子连接。 极性区分了铰链、球关节或固定关节的两个部分，二者必须相反才能连接。 框架是连接器在其零件坐标系中的位置和方向，其中一个轴沿连接方向延伸。 当两个零件实例的兼容连接器对能够对齐至容限范围内时，它们即被视为连接。

paragraphs.en: The connections between instances of an assembly form a graph over parts. An assembly may have more than one component to represent a scene with multiple (disconnected) objects. We define an assembly as stable if it remains at rest under gravity. We treat connected components as rigid bodies of the assembly and simulate them as single rigid bodies of uniform density in PyBullet ( Coumans & Bai, 2016–2021 ) . We set a high coefficient of friction and no restitution, so that inter-component contacts neither slide nor bounce. A component then fails by falling when it is not supported. We consider an assembly stable if no point of any component moves more than three quarters the height of the stud of a brick, 3 LDraw Units (LDU). Effects such as the holding force of stud connections and the play of axles are not modeled, so an assembly that balances as a rigid body passes even when a built one might sag or fall apart. Evaluating this would require a structural simulation, with either a force limit at each connection or a finite-element model of the parts, which we discuss in Sec. 6 . Two parts collide when their geometry overlaps by more than a tolerance. An assembly with collisions cannot be built, and is determined invalid prior to simulation.
paragraphs.zh: 装配体中各个实例之间的连接构成一个基于零件的图。 一个装配体可能包含多个组件，以表示由多个（不相连）对象组成的场景。 如果装配体在重力作用下保持静止，我们便将其定义为稳定。 我们将相连的组件视为装配体的刚体，并在 PyBullet（Coumans & Bai, 2016–2021）中将其模拟为密度均匀的单一刚体。 我们设置较高的摩擦系数且无恢复系数，使组件间的接触既不会滑动也不会弹跳。 当某个组件失去支撑时，它便会因坠落而失效。 如果任何组件上的任意一点移动距离不超过砖块凸台高度的四分之三（即 3 LDraw Units, LDU），我们便认为该装配体是稳定的。 诸如凸台连接的固定力以及轴之间的间隙等效应并未被建模，因此，即使实际搭建的装配体可能会下垂或解体，作为刚体的平衡装配体仍能通过测试。 要对此进行评估，需要进行结构模拟，即对每个连接施加力限制，或对零件进行有限元建模；我们将在第 6 节中讨论这一问题。 当两个零件的几何形状重叠超过容差时，它们会发生碰撞。 存在碰撞的装配体无法被构建，在模拟之前就会被判定为无效。

paragraphs.en: BrickBench is a benchmark of agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a text prompt, an agent must produce an assembly that satisfies semantic and design criteria and that can be physically built. The benchmark consists of 300 prompts in three settings ( Sec. 4.1 ), an environment in which a coding agent can build, and an evaluation protocol for validity, semantic alignment, and design quality ( Sec. 4.4 ). Except for the ablation in Sec. 5.2 and the two data-driven baselines, the agents work inside of the BrickAgent environment described in Sec. 4.3 .
paragraphs.zh: BrickBench 是一个用于智能体文本条件化乐高套装设计的基准测试。 给定一个文本提示，智能体必须生成一个既能满足语义和设计标准，又能实际搭建的组装方案。 该基准测试包含三种设置下的 300 个提示（第 4.1 节）、一个可供编码智能体进行搭建的环境，以及用于评估有效性、语义一致性和设计质量的协议（第 4.4 节）。 除了第 5.2 节中的消融实验和两个数据驱动基线模型外，所有智能体均在第 4.3 节中描述的 BrickAgent 环境中运行。

paragraphs.en: The settings differ in the parts that an agent builds with. In the Model setting, an agent may use at most 400 parts, while the Set setting requires 400–4000 parts be used. Both draw from the full LDraw library as supported by BrickNet, 14,441 part types. paragraphs.en: We decompose each generation prompt into a question graph in the style of DSG ( Cho et al., 2024 ) , which evaluates text-to-image generation by turning a prompt into atomic yes/no questions with an LLM and answering them with a VLM after organizing them by graph dependency. The questions cover the entities named by the prompt, their attributes, and the relations among them. With the graph we can avoid evaluating properties invalidated by other failures, such as checking the color of a knight’s armor when the presence of a knight was not yet established. See Fig. A1 for their distribution by type and Fig. A2 for a full example graph, both in Appendix A .
paragraphs.zh: 我们将每个生成提示分解为一种遵循 DSG（Cho 等人，2024）风格的问答图。该方法通过将提示转化为原子化的“是/否”问题，并利用 LLM 生成这些问题，随后通过 VLM 回答这些经过图依赖关系组织后的问题，从而评估文本到图像的生成效果。这些问题涵盖了提示中命名的实体、它们的属性以及实体之间的关系。借助这种图结构，我们可以避免评估因其他失败而变得无效的属性——例如，在尚未确认是否存在骑士的情况下，就不必检查骑士盔甲的颜色。关于各类问题的分布情况，请参见附录 A 中的图 A1；关于完整的示例图，请参见图 A2。

paragraphs.en: We introduce BrickAgent, an environment in which the agents build. It contains the LDraw library, the BrickNet connector system, and tools for authoring, validating, and viewing an assembly programmatically. The tools include functions to search the library for parts, to place parts by their positions or by connectors, to mirror and measure them, to define subassemblies and combine them, and to render an assembly from any viewpoint. The provided validator includes the connectivity, collision, and stability tests of Sec. 3.2 and interpretably reports each failure with the parts involved. This enables an agent to validate the physical requirements of an assembly prior to submission.
paragraphs.zh: 我们介绍了 BrickAgent，这是一个智能体进行构建的环境。 它包含 LDraw 库、BrickNet 连接器系统，以及用于程序化创建、验证和查看装配的工具。 这些工具包括在库中搜索零件的功能、通过位置或连接器放置零件、镜像和测量零件、定义子装配并组合它们，以及从任意视角渲染装配的功能。 所提供的验证器包含了第 3.2 节中的连通性、碰撞和稳定性测试，并能以可解释的方式报告每个失败及其涉及的零件。 这使得智能体能够在提交之前验证装配的物理要求。

paragraphs.en: VQA measures bounded semantic alignment with the prompt, following DSG. We render the assembly from eight views using BrickNet’s renderer, with consistent render settings. We then ask Gemma 4 31B ( Gemma Team, 2026 ) each question of the graph in one call, with instructions to judge on what the views show and to answer yes or no. The score of an assembly is the fraction of its questions satisfied, and VQA is the mean over assemblies.
paragraphs.zh: 遵循 DSG，VQA 衡量与提示之间的有界语义对齐。 我们使用 BrickNet 的渲染器以一致的渲染设置从八个视角渲染该组合体。 然后，我们通过单次调用向 Gemma 4 31B（Gemma Team，2026）提出图中的每个问题，并指示其根据各视角所显示的内容进行判断，回答“是”或“否”。 一个组合体的得分是其问题中被满足的比例，而 VQA 则是所有组合体得分的平均值。

paragraphs.en: ELO measures relative semantic alignment and design quality against other systems. For each prompt, we form every pairing of assemblies from different systems and show the judge four views of each. We ask two questions of each pair: 1) The alignment question gives the judge the prompt and asks which assembly matches it better. 2) The design question withholds the prompt and asks which assembly is better designed by the standard of an official set, judged on how the pieces are used rather than the subject. Each pair is asked in both orderings to eliminate position bias. Fig. A3 in Appendix B contains the judge prompts. We fit a Bradley–Terry model ( Bradley & Terry, 1952 ) to the wins from each question and report them as ELO. We anchor to a fixed set of references as noted in Sec. 5 . ELO is the average of Align ELO and Design ELO after rescaling to a common spread over the anchors.
paragraphs.zh: ELO 衡量了与其他系统相比的相对语义对齐度和设计质量。 对于每个提示，我们会生成来自不同系统的各个组件组合，并向评审员展示每个组合的四种视图。 我们对每对组合提出两个问题：1) 对齐问题会向评审员提供提示，并询问哪个组合与之更匹配。2) 设计问题则不提供提示，而是询问根据官方标准，哪个组合的设计更优，评判依据是组件的使用方式而非主题。 为避免位置偏差，每对组合都会以两种顺序进行提问。图 B 附录中的 A3 包含了评审员的提示内容。 我们将 Bradley–Terry 模型（Bradley & Terry, 1952）拟合到每个问题中的获胜结果，并将其报告为 ELO。 如第 5 节所述，我们以一组固定的参考项作为基准。 ELO 是对齐 ELO 和设计 ELO 取平均后，再根据基准项重新缩放至共同范围所得的结果。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate eleven agents and two data-driven baselines. The agents include GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, and Muse Spark 1.3. Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 run in Claude Code, and the others in Codex CLI using the vendors’ respective APIs. Astra, both Opus models, and both Sol models are evaluated at high reasoning to bound cost while Luna runs at max and the others at xhigh . Each agent is given a budget of 300 turns per prompt. The baselines evaluated are BrickNet-14B ( Kulits & Schmid, 2026 ) and BrickGPT ( Pun et al., 2025 ) , both restricted to the Model setting which is the only one applicable. Nine of the agents form the reference set of the ELO scale ( Sec. 4.4 ). The baselines and ablated runs of Sec. 5.2 are rated against them and do not affect the scale. paragraphs.en: VQA separates the reference set gently, from 0.59 for GLM to 0.95 for Astra. Design ELO does so more sharply, with 545 ELO points between GLM and Astra, a gap that can be interpreted as a judge preferring Astra’s assembly in around 96% of pairs. Within the reference set, Astra leads on every metric, and Opus 5 is ranked second while incurring four times the cost. Sol, Gemini, Qwen, and DeepSeek form a middle within 41 ELO points of one another. Of the two later agents, GPT-6.1 Sol matches Astra on ELO (1293 against 1297, intervals overlapping) at a fifth of its cost, and Opus 5.5 rates 148 points above Opus 5 at 40% of its cost, inside Astra’s interval on Design ELO but 83 points lower on Align ELO . Alignment varies more with the kind of question than with the subject ( Fig. A7 in Appendix C ). No prompt category is consistently harder than the others, and the two top agents score at least 0.90 in every one. Every agent satisfies at least 91% of the questions about color, but texture is satisfied 49–83% of the time, and object type and state are the next hardest. The stronger agents also build larger and more varied assemblies ( Tab. A1 in Appendix C ). In Model , Astra averages 217 parts of 35 types in 9 colors, and GLM 27 parts of 10 types in 5 colors. In Set , Qwen, DeepSeek, Muse, and GLM average 23 to 40 connected components per assembly, against 2.2 to 4.2 for Astra and both Sol and Opus models, so their scenes consist of far more disconnected pieces. Figs. A4 and A5 in Appendix C plot Tabs. 1 and A1 by setting.
paragraphs.zh: VQA 对参考集的得分差异较为平缓，GLM 为 0.59，Astra 为 0.95。 Design ELO 的区分度则更为显著：GLM 与 Astra 之间的 ELO 分差为 545，这一差距可被解读为在约 96% 的成对比较中，评判者更倾向于选择 Astra 的组合。 在参考集内部，Astra 在所有指标上均领先，而 Opus 5 排名第二，但其成本却是前者的四倍。 Sol、Gemini、Qwen 和 DeepSeek 处于中间水平，彼此之间的 ELO 分差均未超过 41。 在较晚推出的两个智能体中，GPT-6.1 Sol 的 ELO 与 Astra 相当（1293 对 1297，区间重叠），但成本仅为后者的五分之一；Opus 5.5 的评分比 Opus 5 高出 148 分，成本为后者的 40%，其 Design ELO 得分位于 Astra 的区间内，但在 Align ELO 上低了 83 分。 对齐效果因问题类型的不同而差异较大，而非因主题不同（见附录 C 中的图 A7）。 没有任何提示类别的难度持续高于其他类别，且排名最高的两个智能体在所有类别中的得分均至少为 0.90。 所有智能体都能满足至少 91% 的颜色相关问题，但纹理相关问题的满足率仅为 49%–83%，而物体类型和状态则是接下来最难处理的类别。 性能更强的智能体还能构建出规模更大、种类更丰富的组合（见附录 C 中的表 A1）。 在“模型”类别中，Astra 平均每组合包含 217 个部件，涉及 35 种类型和 9 种颜色；GLM 则为 27 个部件，涉及 10 种类型和 5 种颜色。 在“集合”类别中，Qwen、DeepSeek、Muse 和 GLM 平均每组合包含 23 至 40 个连通组件，而 Astra、Sol 和 Opus 模型的平均值仅为 2.2 至 4.2，因此它们所构建的场景由更多互不相连的部件组成。图 A4 和 A5（见附录 C）按设置分别展示了表 1 和表 A1 的数据。

paragraphs.en: To confirm the validity of Design ELO , which rests on a VLM judge, we evaluate against human ratings. We recruit participants on Prolific and show each 40 pairs of same-prompt assemblies, with four views per assembly. We collect 4,080 judgments from 102 raters. We fit the human judgments with the same Bradley–Terry model as ELO ( Sec. 4.4 ), and compare the ratings against Design ELO in Fig. 5(b) . The rankings agree on 34 of the 36 pairs among the agents, with a Kendall τ \tau of 0.89. This follows findings from prior work which demonstrated alignment between VLM and human preferences on text-to-3D generation ( Wu et al., 2024 ) . The judge is more decisive than the rater pool, so we align the two by a constant factor. Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol were released after this study and are not part of it.

paragraphs.en: We asked people familiar with LEGO design to tell agent builds from human ones ( Fig. 6 ). For assemblies in the Model and Set settings, we drew part-count-matched human-designed models from the BrickNet dataset, and asked which of the two a person made. The drawn samples are not prompt-matched. No human designs exist for the BrickBench prompts, so the pairs are matched on part count alone, and Fig. 6(b) shows human models of other subjects. A prompt-matched comparison would require commissioning designs, which we leave to future work. As in Sec. 5.3 , the study predates Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol. Five raters provided 360 ratings altogether, and selected the human model in 323 of them. No agent was taken for a human designer more than one time in five ( Fig. 6(a) ), and every agent’s rate falls significantly below chance. paragraphs.en: We report four findings from our evaluations. First, we find that data-driven models built for the task are subsumed by general agents. A general coding agent exceeds models on their own benchmark ( Sec. 3.3 ) and on ours. Cost, however, remains an axis for future work. BrickNet-14B produces an assembly for six hundredths of a cent, while the Astra does so in $4.06. Second, prompt adherence saturates. The best-performing agent satisfies 95% of the VQA questions asked of it, and absolute alignment does not strongly separate the top performers. Headroom lies instead in design quality. Third, agent performance is dependent on the environment. The same model produces consistently buildable assemblies with BrickAgent, and unbuildable ones without it ( Tab. 2 ). Fourth, a gap remains to humans. Participants familiar with LEGO design filtered agent-designed assemblies from human ones nine out of ten times ( Fig. 6 ). We interpret this as a measure of design quality: agents satisfy requirements but fall short of the standards of a designed set.
paragraphs.zh: 我们报告了评估中得出的四项发现。 首先，我们发现为该项任务构建的数据驱动模型已被通用智能体所超越。 一款通用编码智能体在其自身的基准测试（第 3.3 节）以及我们的基准测试中都优于这些模型。 然而，成本仍然是未来研究的一个关键维度。 BrickNet-14B 的组装成本仅为六百分之一美分，而 Astra 的成本则为 4.06 美元。 其次，提示词遵循性存在饱和现象。 表现最佳的智能体能够回答其提出的 VQA 问题的 95%，而绝对的指令对齐并未显著区分出顶尖模型。 真正的提升空间反而在于设计质量。 第三，智能体的性能取决于其所处的环境。 同一模型在配合 BrickAgent 时能持续生成可组装的结构，而在没有它时则无法做到（表 2）。 第四，与人类相比仍存在差距。 熟悉乐高设计的参与者在十次尝试中有九次能够区分出智能体设计的结构与人类设计的结构（图 6）。 我们将此视为设计质量的衡量标准：智能体能够满足需求，但尚未达到精心设计套装的标准。

paragraphs.en: We introduced BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. The domain gives the task a floor that a simulator can verify and an open ceiling on design quality. It includes 300 prompts in three settings with different constraints, a reference environment in which agents build, BrickAgent, and a set of metrics that score build validity, alignment, and design confirmed by human raters. Nine frontier agents build valid assemblies for most prompts and satisfy the majority of what each requests, displacing task-specific data-driven models at an increase of 900–6,800 times the cost. While doing so, we highlight the open challenge of narrowing the gap to human design.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 BrickBench，一个用于智能体文本条件化乐高套装设计的基准测试。 该领域为任务设定了模拟器可以验证的最低标准，同时为设计质量保留了开放的上限。 它包含三种不同设置下的 300 个提示词，每种设置都有不同的约束条件；还包括一个供智能体构建的参考环境 BrickAgent，以及一套由人类评估者确认的指标，用于评分构建的有效性、一致性和设计。 九款前沿智能体能够针对大多数提示词构建出有效的组合结构，并满足大部分需求，以仅增加 900 至 6,800 倍的成本取代了任务特定的数据驱动模型。 在此过程中，我们强调了缩小与人类设计之间差距这一开放挑战。

sents.zh: 对齐提示包含该提示，并询问无论其构建质量如何，哪个装配覆盖了其中更多内容。

sents.en: The design prompt withholds the prompt and asks which assembly is better designed, whatever it depicts.
sents.zh: 设计提示则不透露该提示，而是询问无论其描绘内容如何，哪个装配的设计更优。

sents.en: The VQA prompt lists every question of the graph, tells the judge to answer from the views alone, and requires a yes or a no on each.
sents.zh: VQA 提示列出了图中的所有问题，要求裁判仅根据视图作答，并对每个问题给出“是”或“否”的答案。
